title: Body Asymmetry
author: Cristina Zogmaister

steps_raw.instruction: Measuring Objectification Through the Body Inversion Paradigm: Methodological Issues Cristina Zogmaister, Federica Durante, Silvia Mari, Franca Crippa, and Chiara Volpato University of Milano-Bicocca Corresponding author: Cristina Zogmaister E-mail: cristina.zogmaister@unimib.it (CZ) Protocol	for	the	computation	of	Asymmetry	Body	Posture	Index;	ABPI Abstract	This	protocol	describes	the	algorithm	that	we	used	to	measure	the	asymmetry	of	images	of	body	shapes.	The	SPSS	syntax	for	the	computation	of	asymmetry	is	provided. The	postural	asymmetry	of	each	picture	is	based	on	the	following	parts	of	the	body: 1. chin	2. navel	3. top	of	the	head	4. elbows	5. shoulders	6. hips 7. hands	8. legs The	index	takes	into	account	the	Cartesian	distance	from	the	vertical	line	in	the	center	of	the	image	in	the	case	of	unique	points	(chin,	navel,	forehead).	In	the	case	of	double	points	(elbows,	shoulders,	hips,	hands,	legs),	the	Cartesian	distance	between	the	right	point	and	the	mirror	image	of	the	left	point	is	taken	into	consideration. In	order	to	compute	the	asymmetry	index	of	an	image,	the	rater	has	to	measure	the	following	points	in	pixels:

x1:	top	of	the	head; x2:	chin; x3:	navel; (x4a,	y4a):	left	elbow;	(x4b,	y4b):	right	elbow;	(x5a,	y5a):	left	shoulder;	(x5b,	y5b):	right	shoulder;	(x6a,	y6a):	left	hip;	(x6b,	y6b):	right	hip;	(x7a,	y7a):	left	hand,	end	of	middle	fingertip;	(x7b,	y7b):	right	hand,	end	of	middle	fingertip;	(x8a,	y8a):	external	part	of	the	left	leg,	where	it	touches	the	border	of	the	image;	(x8b,	y8b):	external	part	of	the	right	leg,	where	it	touches	the	border	of	the	image. Then	the	rater	reports	these	positions	in	pixels	in	a	spreadsheet. The	algorithm	consists	in	the	following	passages: 1) computation	of	the	X	coordinate	of	the	center	of	the	body	shape	–	which	is	operationalized	as	follows:	a. the	center	is	computed	for	each	double	point,	as	average	of	the	X	value	for	the	left	and	for	the	right	points	(e.g.,	the	center	for	the	elbows	is	computed	as	the	average	between	x4a	and	x4b) b. the	average	of	the	X	value	is	computed	based	on	the	eight	different	parts	of	the	body	and	this	average	is	considered	as	the	X	coordinate	of	the	center	of	the	body	shape	2) computation	of	a	partial	asymmetry	index	for	each	of	the	eight	body	parts:	a. for	the	three	unique	points,	compute	the	values	dist1,	dist2,	and	dist3	as	distances	between	the	measured	points	and	the	center;	b. for	the	five	double	points,	compute	the	X	coordinate	of	the	mirror	image,	mirrored	on	the	center	as	computed	in	(a);	c. for	the	five	double	points,	compute	the	values	dist4,	dist5,	dist6,	dist7,	and	dist8;	each	represents	the	distance	between	the	coordinates	(xa,	ya)	and	(xbspecular,	yb);	3) computation	of	the	overall	asymmetry	index	as	sum	of	all	eight	distances	computed	in	(2).	Therefore,	for	each	image	a	single	value	(i.e.,	Asymmetry	Body	Posture	Index;	ABPI)	is	obtained	that	summarized	the	overall	degree	of	postural	asymmetry.	Higher	values	correspond	to	higher	levels	of	asymmetry.

Please	find	the	SPSS	syntax	for	the	computation	of	asymmetry	hereafter:	*** SPSS	syntax	for	the	computation	of	the	asymmetry	index ***	Measuring	Objectification	Through	the	Body	Inversion	Paradigm:	Methodological	Issues **	computation	of	the	vertical	X	axis	-	the	center	of	the	image	**	COMPUTE	Xcenter	=	mean	(X1,X2,X3,	mean(X4a,	X4b),	mean(X5a,	X5b),	mean(X6a,	X6b),	mean(X7a,	X7b),	mean(X8a,	X8b)). EXECUTE. **	computation	of	the	distance	between	the	unique	points	and	the	center	of	the	image	**	COMPUTE	dist1=abs(X1-Xcenter).	COMPUTE	dist2=abs(X2-Xcenter).	COMPUTE	dist3=abs(X3-Xcenter). **	computation	of	the	specular	points	**	compute	x4b_s	=	Xcenter	*	2	-	x4b.	compute	x5b_s	=	Xcenter	*	2	-	x5b.	compute	x6b_s	=	Xcenter	*	2	-	x6b.	compute	x7b_s	=	Xcenter	*	2	-	x7b.	compute	x8b_s	=	Xcenter	*	2	-	x8b. **	computation	of	cartesian	distances	**	compute	dist4=sqrt((x4a-x4b_s)*(	x4a-x4b_s)+(y4a-y4b)*(y4a-y4b)).	compute	dist5=sqrt((x5a-x5b_s)*(	x5a-x5b_s)+(y5a-y5b)*(y5a-y5b)).	compute	dist6=sqrt((x6a-x6b_s)*(	x6a-x6b_s)+(y6a-y6b)*(y6a-y6b)).	compute	dist7=sqrt((x7a-x7b_s)*(	x7a-x7b_s)+(y7a-y7b)*(y7a-y7b)).	compute	dist8=sqrt((x8a-x8b_s)*(	x8a-x8b_s)+(y8a-y8b)*(y8a-y8b)).	EXECUTE. **	computation	of	asymmetry	as	sum	of	the	indicators	COMPUTE	asymmetry=sum(dist1,	dist2,dist3,dist4,dist5,dist6,dist7,dist8).	EXECUTE.
